text:
alex: Heads up — seeing multiple GPU nodes in ap-southeast-2 fail during bootstrap. Error is KMS timeout when trying to unwrap instance keys. Started ~09:10 UTC, ~30 nodes impacted.
mira: :rotating_light: can you paste the bootstrap logs?
alex: pasted below
```
2026-03-18T09:11:02Z kubelet[1]: ERROR: failed to decrypt bootstrap key: context deadline exceeded dialing kms.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com:443
...
```
samir: infra-bot alert showed a spike in tcp resets to KMS from the GPU-subnet NAT. Could be egress ACL or managed prefix list change earlier.
infra-bot: ALERT: 1958001111-A — 30 instances failing KMS unwrap; high sfr. Detected egress policy update at 2026-03-18T08:55:12Z by beatrice.
beatrice: I applied a tighter egress rule to the GPU subnets to block unknown destinations. I didn't expect KMS to be affected, thought kms endpoints are in the managed prefix list. listing the rule: `deny all outbound except PL-RELIABLE, S3, CONTROL_PLANE`
mira: @beatrice can you revert the rule or add kms endpoints to the allowlist? Compliance asked for the deny-first change but we need a fast mitigation.
beatrice: rolling back now to previous rule — doing `terraform apply` (small change). ETA ~5m.
alex: meanwhile nodes are stuck in CrashLoopBackoff on init. Any way to force them to use a local key or fallback?
samir: we can temporarily attach the fallback KMS key via instance profile but that needs role changes and would require KMS grant. Probably slower than rollback.
mira: quick patch: allowlist `kms.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com` on egress for GPU subnets (works as a quick fix, but we should prefer PL).
beatrice: rollback completed. Confirming with `aws ec2 describe-security-group-rules --group-id sg-0abc` shows previous egress restored.
infra-bot: INFO: egress-rule-reconcile completed by beatrice at 2026-03-18T09:16:05Z. Monitoring KMS connectivity.
alex: nodes started rejoining k8s at 09:17 and bootstraps succeeded. Partial recovery confirmed, +28 of 30 rejoined.
mira: follow-ups: 1) add KMS managed prefix list to our allowed PL-RELIABLE mapping 2) add an e2e test for KMS unwrap in the GPU pool during infra PRs 3) audit trail: annotate the terraform change with compliance justification.
samir: also we should consider PrivateLink for KMS or VPC endpoints instead of wide egress. That removes public egress dependency and reduces blast radius. Cost tradeoff: NAT egress vs interface endpoints — interface endpoints in ap-southeast-2 are ~0.02/hr each + data processing. We should model for our peak GPU bandwidth.
beatrice: noted. I'll open a follow-up ticket and a PR linking cost model. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2245
alex: good call. Also: add an audit log event referencing this incident to the compliance channel and tag the KMS key rotation policy so it doesn't auto-rotate mid-change.
mira: opened runbook entry: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-kms-egress.md and added proactive tests to ci.
beatrice: :thumbsup: will schedule a gated rollout of the deny-first egress rules with a canary that excludes GPU subnets until we have PrivateLink.
infra-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: 1958001111 — root cause: overly restrictive egress ACL applied to GPU subnets blocking KMS endpoints. Remediation: rollback and add allowlist; follow-ups created: INFRA-1023 (PrivateLink evaluation), INFRA-1024 (e2e KMS test), INFRA-1025 (terraform change audit).
